title: AUCTIONS OF MEMENTOS AND GIFTS PRESENTED TO PRIME MINISTER
body_text:
The details of the amount received by the Government through the auction of mementos and gifts presented to the Hon’ble Prime Minister are as under:
1 st Edition (2021)      :  Rs. 3.1 Cr
2 nd Edition (2022)     :  Rs. 3.6 Cr
3 rd Edition (2023)     :   Rs. 15.8 Cr
4 th Edition (2023)      :   Rs. 14.4 Cr
5 th Edition (2024)      :   Rs. 11.16 Cr
6 th Edition (2024)      :   Rs.  2.24 Cr
7 th Edition (2025)      :    Rs. 1.89 Cr
The dates/period on which e-auctions of mementos and gifts were organized during the last five years are as follows:
2021    : 17 th September to 7 th October
2022    : 17 th September to 12 th October
2023    : 17 th September to 31 st October
2024    : 17 th September to 31 st October
2025    : 17 th September to 31 st October
Before 2019, no auction of mementos and gifts was organized by the National Gallery of Modern Arts (NGMA).
This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today
***
M Annadurai

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Culture informed Lok Sabha that e-auctions of mementos and gifts presented to the Prime Minister have raised over Rs. 52 crore across seven editions since 2021, organized annually by the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) typically from 17th September onwards. Proceeds ranged from Rs. 1.89 crore to a peak of Rs. 15.8 crore in the 3rd edition (2023). The Minister clarified that no such auctions were held before 2019.
enrichment.context: The auction of mementos and gifts received by the Prime Minister is part of an initiative aimed at promoting public engagement with symbolic items associated with the Prime Minister's Office while channeling proceeds towards public welfare causes, notably the Namami Gange programme for cleaning the Ganga river. These auctions, conducted online, have been held annually around Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October) since 2019, coinciding with themes of austerity and public contribution to national causes. The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Culture, has been entrusted with organizing these auctions, showcasing gifts ranging from paintings and handicrafts to personal memorabilia given to the PM during official engagements. This initiative reflects a broader push towards transparency in the use of state gifts and reinforces symbolic messaging around simplicity in public office, while also generating non-tax revenue for designated welfare schemes.

prelims_questions.question: The e-auction of mementos and gifts received by the Prime Minister of India is organized by which of the following institutions?
options: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) has been organizing the e-auctions of mementos and gifts presented to the Prime Minister.

prelims_questions.question: According to a recent Lok Sabha reply, no auction of mementos and gifts presented to the Prime Minister was organized before which year?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that before 2019, no auction of mementos and gifts was organized by NGMA.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of auctioning state gifts and mementos received by public office holders in India. How does such practice reflect on transparency, accountability, and public welfare financing?
Examine the role of cultural institutions like the National Gallery of Modern Art in supporting government initiatives beyond their traditional mandate of art preservation and exhibition.
